tokyo_gonpachi_asakusa_azumaba.price_note: No dish and no price — an honest empty reached after downloading everything the shop publishes. 権八 puts its entire menu online as FIVE PDFs (grand menu, weekday lunch, holiday lunch, drinks, party plans) and all five were fetched and run through a text extractor. Every one is a pure IMAGE SCAN: they yield between 1 and 10 characters each. Nothing — not a dish, not a price, not a section heading — is machine-readable in any of them. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THIS IS NOW THE FOURTH OPERATOR IN THIS DATASET TO PUBLISH A COMPLETE MENU IN A FORM NO READER CAN USE, after RAKERU’s scanned grand menu, 俺の割烹’s bilingual PDF that lost its Japanese and every price, and ニューヨーカーズカフェ’s 1.8MB allergen table that extracts one character. The pattern is worth stating plainly: a restaurant that publishes a scan has disclosed nothing to anyone who cannot see the image — which includes screen-reader users and every automated allergen check, not only this project. ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THIS KITCHEN SERVES IS RECORDED, deliberately. Gonpachi is a well-known izakaya brand and it would be easy to write down what such a place "obviously" has; that is exactly the reasoning this dataset forbids. Re-check if the operator ever publishes an HTML menu, or when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_torinao.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop’s site is a JavaScript application — a Nuxt build whose served HTML contains the shop name, the Tawaramachi location and the page shell, and no menu content at all. Both the root and the /menu/ path were fetched directly and rendered through a text-extracting fetcher, and neither yields an item. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THIS KITCHEN SERVES IS RECORDED, deliberately, and it is worth naming what is being withheld: 鳥 in the name means chicken, and a Japanese chicken restaurant turns on exactly one question a coeliac needs answered — タレ or 塩. A tare is soy, mirin and sugar, painted on during grilling and absorbed; salt is salt. That single distinction decides most of a yakitori board, and it is unanswerable from a page that renders nothing. Reading it off the shop name would be the error this dataset forbids. Re-check when the site serves HTML, or when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_kayu_sanchin_okayu_to_me.price_note: ⚠ NO PRICES ARE RECORDED HERE AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the operator publishes a full allergen table and a full nutrition table but no price list anywhere on its site, so every price below is deliberately empty rather than invented. What it does publish is worth far more than prices. The allergen sheet is dated 二〇二四年十二月更新 and is explicitly scoped to 「粥餐庁　京王モール、仙台エスパル店、KITTE博多店、札幌オーロラタウン店」 — the Keio Mall branch this record covers is named on it, so this is the right branch, not a chain-wide approximation. ⚠ THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE FINDING IN THIS TICK AND IT INVERTS WHAT EVERYONE ASSUMES. Rice congee is the food people reach for when they are ill, when they are avoiding gluten, when they want the plainest possible thing in the bowl. At 粥餐庁 the PLAIN CONGEE BASE — 素かゆ, the bare porridge with nothing added — declares 小麦・乳成分・えび・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉. Wheat, milk AND shrimp are in the base itself. The sheet then says so explicitly: 「＊ベースのおかゆのみのアレルギーとなります。すべてのおかゆに含まれております」 — this applies to EVERY congee on the menu. There is no okayu here that a coeliac can eat, and no topping choice changes that, because the wheat is in the pot before anything is added. ⚠ THE REASON IS IN THE SHOP'S OWN DESCRIPTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS WORTH UNDERSTANDING RATHER THAN JUST RECORDING. Chinese congee is not Japanese okayu. The shop explains that 中国粥 is cooked from raw rice in boiling STOCK rather than water — 「毎朝熱々の自家製スープで生米から毎日じっくり炊き上げる」 — so the porridge is built on a house soup, and that soup is where the chicken, pork, shrimp and wheat come from. The 粥たれ served with it is separately described as カキとカツオと昆布, oyster, bonito and kombu. A Japanese okayu is rice and water; this is rice and broth, and the difference is the whole answer. ⚠ THE VEGAN TRAP IS JUST AS SHARP: ８種野菜のベジかゆ, the eight-vegetable "veggie congee", declares 乳成分・えび・鶏肉・豚肉 — milk, shrimp, chicken and pork. A dish named for being vegetable-based contains four animal ingredients, because it inherits the same stock. ⚠ THE NOODLES ARE NOT AN ESCAPE EITHER, AND ONE WORD ON THE SITE WILL MISLEAD PEOPLE: the shop advertises 全粒粉麺, wholemeal noodles. Wholemeal is wheat. Every noodle dish declares 卵・小麦, and 濃厚ごま担々麺 adds 落花生 (peanut). ⚠ WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN, BY THE SHOP'S OWN TABLE, IS A SHORT LIST AND IT IS ALL SIDES AND DRINKS: 青菜 and みょうが・三つ葉・パクチー are marked 「アレルギーは含まれておりません」 outright, 鮭 declares さけ only, 杏仁豆腐 declares 乳成分・大豆 with no wheat, and ウーロン茶, ジャスミン茶 and コーヒー declare nothing at all. ⚠ AND THE SHEET CARRIES TWO WARNINGS THAT MATTER: 「また調理器具は同一のものを使用しております」 — the same cooking equipment is used throughout — and the 肉まん lines add 「＊卵・えび・かに・いか・ゼラチンが混入している可能性があります」, a declared possibility of cross-contamination with egg, shrimp, crab, squid and gelatin. The chain dates to a 1967 founding philosophy of 医食同源 and opened as 謝朋殿 粥餐庁 in Shinjuku in March 2001; the congee is a 白米2:玄米1 blend.

tokyo_mita_seimenjo_suidobashi.price_note: PARTIAL FOR ONE SPECIFIC REASON: 三田製麺所's official menu page names and describes every item on the card but prints NO PRICES ANYWHERE — not on the category page and not on the top page. The item list below is therefore complete and first-party, and the price field is deliberately empty on every row rather than filled from a third party. The dataset's own menu_url for this record points at Tabelog, which this egress cannot reach (Cloudflare challenge since 2026-09-02), so no price cross-check was possible. Anyone with Tabelog access can fill the prices in without re-doing the item work. Note also that mita-seimen.com/en/2018/07/13/shop_29_suidoubashi/ — the URL this dataset carries as the shop's website — now 404s; the chain has restructured its site and the branch page no longer exists at that path, so the record is keyed to the chain menu. ⚠ THIS IS A TSUKEMEN SPECIALIST AND IT IS A FLAT NO FOR A COELIAC. The shop's name literally means "Mita noodle factory"; the whole proposition is thick wheat 極太麺. tokyo_udagawa_naru.price_note: NEARLY AN EMPTY, AND THE ONE ITEM BELOW IS PROSE RATHER THAN A MENU. ウダガワ 成ル's official site is a single WordPress page carrying the address (渋谷区宇田川町6-20 パラシオン渋谷1F), the phone (03-3461-1166), hours 17:30–23:00, 定休日 不定休, a Google map and an Instagram embed that returns 投稿はありません — no posts. There is no menu page, no PDF, no price list and no 品書き anywhere on the site; the nav is HOME / GOOGLE MAP / OFFICIAL only. The single dish recorded below is named in the shop's own descriptive paragraph, not on a menu, and carries no price — it is included because it is genuinely first-party evidence of what the kitchen serves, and excluded from any price claim. The shop's sister venues (氣ウラ, 巖 渋谷, ミヤシタ成ル) are separate records and their pages were not used here. The dataset's menu_url points at Tabelog, which this egress cannot reach. ⚠ WHAT THE SITE DOES TELL A COELIAC: the shop describes itself as 鉄板焼き — teppanyaki — with 和食をベースにしたさまざまな一品料理 and a large regional sake list. A teppan is a single shared steel plate on which soy-based sauces are used all evening, which is about the least separable cooking surface there is. Treat the whole venue as ask-at-best and expect no allergen sheet.

items.en: Rolled dashi omelette (changes daily)
items.note: ⚠ Named by the shop as its 日替わりの (daily-changing) teppanyaki item. Japanese dashimaki is seasoned with 白だし or めんつゆ, both soy-sauce products and therefore wheat, and the dashi itself is bonito — so this is both a gluten fact and a non-vegan one. Price not published.

tokyo_sacya_shibuya_scramble_s.price_note: SACYA'S SITE IS LIVE AND PUBLISHES NO MENU. Both the Shibuya Scramble Square shop page and the company's /cafe/ index were fetched and read in full: they give the address (B2F, Shibuya Scramble Square, 2-24-12 Shibuya) and postcode and nothing else about what is served — no drink list, no prices, no PDF, no allergen note. The /menu/ path was probed and 404s. The site's ONLINE STORE panel reads 「coming soon.」 and its store.sacya.jp link was not used, because a retail bean/leaf shop is not this café's counter menu and quoting it here would attach the wrong prices to the record. The company's other listed location, SACYA 代官山, is explicitly marked 「※現在リニューアルに向けて閉業中」 — closed for renovation — which is a useful signal that the site IS maintained, and therefore that the absence of a menu is a choice rather than neglect. The dataset's menu_url is Tabelog, unreachable from this egress. SACYA is recorded as a matcha specialty café; a matcha stand is a genuinely promising GF and vegan candidate (whisked tea is neither wheat nor dairy, and plant milks are common), so this record is worth finishing when a menu source appears — but nothing has been established here.

tokyo_tempura_shinjuku_tsunaha.price_note: つな八'S OWN PAGE FOR 総本店別館 WAS FETCHED AND READ IN FULL AND IT DESCRIBES ITS COURSES WITHOUT NAMING OR PRICING THEM — the course titles and the per-course prices are set as images, so what survives as text is the composition of each course and nothing else. Those compositions are recorded below verbatim because they are genuinely useful (they tell you how many fried items and of what kind), but no course here has a name or a price and none has been invented. The only figures on the page are 平均予算: 2,500円 at lunch and 5,000円 at dinner. 総本店別館 is 新宿3-28-4 TRES SHINJUKU 6F・B1F, open 11:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00), 35 seats on 6F and 34 in the basement, all non-smoking. Lunch courses run to 15:00 (L.O. 15:00) per a 2026/07/07 notice. ⚠ THE ONE PIECE OF REAL ALLERGEN INFORMATION ON THE WHOLE SITE IS THE FRYING OIL, AND IT IS FIRST-PARTY: 「天ぷら新宿つな八 の天ぷら油は創業以来ヘルシーなごま油を使用しています」 — the shop has fried in SESAME OIL since it was founded. Sesame is one of Japan's statutory allergen items and this is a whole-restaurant, every-dish fact, so anyone with a sesame allergy cannot eat here at all. It is the single most valuable line recovered from this record. ⚠ THE /calorie/ PAGE IS NOT AN ALLERGEN TABLE. It exists, it is titled カロリー情報, and its actual table is an image; the page's only readable content is the sesame-oil sentence and a citation to a 2009 Takahashi Shoten calorie dictionary. ⚠ TEMPURA IS WHEAT AND THERE IS NO VERSION OF THIS MEAL THAT IS NOT. Every course is a run of items fried in a wheat-flour-and-egg batter in shared oil, and the 天つゆ served with it is dashi, mirin and soy sauce — so each course is recorded no on both axes. お揃い at the end of each composition is the rice, miso soup and pickles that close a tempura course; the miso soup is dashi-based and the pickles are usually soy-cured.

tokyo_yokohama_iekei_ramen_sam.price_note: ⚠ THE MENU BELOW IS USER-SUBMITTED, NOT THE SHOP’S OWN BOARD, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO KNOW ABOUT IT. Yahoo! Map heads this list ユーザー投稿のメニュー — items photographed and typed in by members of the public — and prints its own disclaimer, ※ 掲載時点の情報です。最新情報は店舗でご確認ください. Nothing here is dated. Some entries are visibly other diners’ shorthand rather than menu lines. It is recorded because it is the only itemised, priced list that exists for this shop on any page reachable from here, and because the dish names themselves are informative; treat every figure as approximate and every spelling as a diner’s. One entry on the list is literally 「ーめん」 at 850円 — a diner’s dropped character for らーめん — which is as clear a demonstration as you could ask for of what kind of list this is. The shop’s own listed channel is X (twitter.com/samurai_EAK), which returned a page to this egress but no menu; a second aggregator, gourmet.tsuku2.jp, timed out. Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT 家系 (IEKEI) MEANS, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICES: Yokohama iekei ramen is a defined style, not a shop’s invention — a broth of PORK BONE AND CHICKEN together, a soy-sauce tare, thick short-cut wheat noodles, and a fixed topping set of spinach, a sheet or three of nori and a slice of chashu. Every one of those five components is either animal or wheat, and the two combine: the tare is soy (wheat), the noodle is wheat, the broth is pork and chicken. There is no iekei bowl anywhere that is vegetarian and none that is gluten-free. The customisation an iekei counter offers — 麺の硬さ (noodle firmness), 味の濃さ (tare strength), 油の量 (fat) — adjusts how much of the soy tare and back-fat goes in, so 薄め means less wheat seasoning but never none. ⚠ THE RICE IS THE POINT AND IT IS ALSO THE ONE NON-WHEAT ITEM. Rice at 100円 and half-rice below it are on this list because eating iekei with rice is the ritual: you dunk the nori in the broth and wrap it round rice. A plain bowl of unseasoned rice is the only thing here without wheat in it — until the broth goes on it, which is the entire reason it was ordered.

items.en: The standard bowl — Yokohama iekei: pork-bone-and-chicken broth, soy tare, thick straight noodles, spinach, nori and chashu. Also typed by one diner as 「ーめん」 at the same 850円, which is the same bowl
items.note: 家系＝豚骨＋鶏がら、醤油ダレ、太麺。All three fail at once: pork and chicken bones in the broth, wheat soy in the tare, wheat in the noodle. The standing toppings add chashu (pork, soy-braised) and nori. Adjusting 味の濃さ to 薄め reduces the soy but does not remove it.

items.en: The bowl with extra nori — at an iekei shop this is a real order, not a garnish, because the nori is what you wrap the rice in
items.note: 海苔自体は海藻だが、味付海苔なら醤油。The seaweed is the plant part; whether it carries soy of its own depends on which kind the shop buys, and it is going into a pork-and-chicken broth regardless.

items.en: A bowl of plain white rice — the standard iekei accompaniment and, at 100 yen, the cheapest thing on the counter
items.note: THE ONLY ITEM IN THE BUILDING WITHOUT WHEAT IN IT. Plain unseasoned Japanese rice — not takikomi, not fried, which are the two ways a rice bowl normally picks up soy sauce. Kept at ask rather than better because this is a wheat kitchen with no allergen policy, the scoop is shared, and the rice is handed across a counter where wheat noodles are being drained. And note what it is for: iekei rice exists to be soaked in the broth.

items.en: Half portion of plain rice
items.price: 未掲載 (not published — listed by a diner without a figure)
items.note: Same plain rice, half the bowl. Also recorded as a combination, ラーメン＋半ライス, in Yahoo’s 〜999円 band.

items.en: Soft-boiled seasoned egg, as a topping
items.note: 味付＝醤油ダレ漬け＝小麦。“Seasoned” means marinated in soy sauce, so the egg is a wheat item in its own right. Egg.

items.en: Everything-on — the loaded bowl with the full topping set. Recorded by a diner under the mistyped name 前乗せ in Yahoo’s 1,000円〜 band
items.note: More chashu, more nori, more egg — every one of them soy-marinated. The loaded bowl is the most wheat-exposed order on the counter.

tokyo_taiwan_tonyu_daiou_taiwa.price_note: ⚠ THE MENU BELOW IS USER-SUBMITTED, NOT THE SHOP’S OWN BOARD. Yahoo! Map heads this list ユーザー投稿のメニュー — items typed in by members of the public — and prints its own disclaimer, ※ 掲載時点の情報です。最新情報は店舗でご確認ください. Nothing here is dated, and the transliterations are diners’ own. One entry below is recorded as 誠豆ハセット, which is a diner mangling 鹹豆漿セット — useful confirmation of what kind of list this is. Hitosara was read and confirms the shop but publishes no menu: it gives ランチ ～999円, ディナー 4,000〜4,999円, and 定休日 日曜日、祝日 (closed Sundays and public holidays). Gnavi was read and carries no prices at all. Instagram is the shop’s only live channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. Note that this shop sits by Kudanshita/Jimbōchō rather than at Suidōbashi proper, despite where the record files it — the Tabelog id on file (13246735) matches the Hitosara listing, so it is the same business. ⚠ WHY A TAIWANESE BREAKFAST SHOP IS ONE OF THE BEST ENTRIES IN THIS DATASET FOR A PLANT-EATER AND ONE OF THE WORST FOR A COELIAC. Taiwanese breakfast is built on SOY MILK, and 豆漿 — sweet soy milk, 480円 here — is soybeans and water and sugar and nothing else: vegan, wheat-free, and served hot in a bowl. 豆花, the soft soy pudding, is the same base set soft. Those two are genuinely clean. Almost everything else on the list is wheat, and it is wheat in forms a European will not recognise: 胡椒餅 is a BAKED WHEAT BUN with pork and pepper inside, 蛋餅 (danbing) is a WHEAT-FLOUR crêpe rolled round egg, and 鹹豆漿 — the savoury soy milk that is the shop’s namesake dish — is conventionally served with a torn 油條, a deep-fried WHEAT dough stick, dropped into it. The soy milk is safe; the thing floating in it is not. ⚠ AND ONE GENUINE SURPRISE: 肉圓 (bawan) is the one Taiwanese street food whose wrapper is NOT wheat — it is a translucent skin made from sweet-potato starch and rice flour. That makes it the only savoury item here that could be available to a coeliac, and it comes with a sauce, and the sauce is the question.

items.en: Soy milk — the shop is named for it (豆乳大王, “soy milk king”). Served hot, freshly ground, sweet by default; this is what Taiwan drinks at breakfast
items.note: THE CLEANEST ITEM IN THE SHOP. 豆漿は大豆・水・砂糖のみ。Soybeans, water and sugar — no wheat ingredient, no animal ingredient, and no seasoning stage where either could enter. Soy is itself one of Japan’s recommended-declaration allergens, so this is the one thing here a soy-allergic traveller must avoid rather than seek.

items.en: Soy milk set — the soy milk with something to eat alongside it
items.note: What comes with it is not published, and that is the whole gluten question: at a Taiwanese breakfast counter the default accompaniment is 油條, a fried WHEAT dough stick, or a 蛋餅, a wheat crêpe. Ask what the set contains before assuming the drink’s cleanliness carries over.

items.ja: 鹹豆漿セット（ミニ魯肉飯付）
items.en: Savoury soy milk set with a small lu rou fan — recorded by a diner as 誠豆ハセット ミニ魯肉飯. Shentoujiang is soy milk set into loose curds with vinegar, seasoned savoury rather than sweet
items.note: 鹹豆漿は台湾では油條（小麦の揚げパン）と干し海老・菜脯を載せるのが定番。THE NAMESAKE DISH AND IT IS NOT THE SAFE ONE. The soy-milk base is clean; the standard toppings are not — a torn deep-fried wheat cruller, and commonly dried shrimp and preserved radish. The 魯肉飯 in the set is pork braised in soy sauce, so wheat and pork again. Neither component is declared here.

items.en: Lu rou fan — minced pork belly braised down in soy, five-spice and rock sugar, ladled over rice. Taiwan’s national comfort dish
items.note: 魯肉は醤油で煮込む＝小麦。The braise is soy sauce, and the pork sits in it rather than beside it, so there is no version without. Pork.

items.ja: 魯肉飯＆鶏肉飯（ハーフ＆ハーフ）
items.en: Half and half — braised pork rice on one side, poached-chicken rice on the other
items.note: 鶏肉飯は鶏の茹で汁と鶏油をかける＝油そのものは小麦不使用だが、たれは醤油。The chicken side is shredded poached chicken with rendered chicken fat and the poaching liquor over rice, which is closer to wheat-free than the pork side — but it is finished with a soy-based sauce and nothing here is declared. Pork and chicken.

items.en: Lu rou fan as a set. Also recorded as 魯肉飯セット ミニ豆漿 — with a small soy milk
items.note: Soy-braised pork over rice with a drink. The mini 豆漿 version is the one to take if you want the clean drink with it.

items.en: Chicken rice set with a danbing — recorded by a diner as 鶏肉飯セット 蛋餅
items.note: 蛋餅の皮は小麦粉。The danbing is the problem: its skin is a wheat-flour batter crêpe, rolled around egg. Chicken, egg and wheat in one set.

items.en: Danbing — a thin savoury crêpe cooked with egg spread over it and rolled up. The other pillar of Taiwanese breakfast alongside soy milk
items.note: 蛋餅の生地は小麦粉と水。The pancake is wheat flour and water, and 蛋 means egg — both are the dish rather than an addition. Frequently served with a sweetened soy dipping sauce as well.

items.en: Pepper bun — a fist-sized bun of pork and black pepper and spring onion, slapped onto the inside wall of a clay oven and baked until the outside blisters. Taipei night-market food
items.note: 胡椒餅の皮は小麦粉の生地。The shell is a wheat dough — this is a baked bun, and the crust is the point of it. Pork inside, seasoned with soy.

items.en: Bawan — a translucent dumpling the size of a fist, steamed then warmed in oil, with pork and bamboo shoot inside, eaten under a sweet-and-savoury sauce
items.note: ⚠ THE ONE SAVOURY ITEM HERE WHOSE WRAPPER IS NOT WHEAT. 肉圓の皮はサツマイモ澱粉と米粉で作る＝小麦不使用。The translucent skin is sweet-potato starch and rice flour, which is exactly why it looks like nothing else on a wheat-heavy menu. That makes the SAUCE the deciding question, and the sauce is not declared: Taiwanese bawan sauce is normally a rice-and-starch paste with sugar and often a soy or fermented-bean element. Worth asking about properly. Pork.

items.en: Congee — rice porridge, the third leg of a Taiwanese breakfast
items.note: 台湾粥は干し椎茸・干し海老・肉のいずれかで炊くのが一般的。Rice and water carry no wheat, but the interesting question at a Taiwanese counter is what the porridge was cooked IN — dried shiitake, dried shrimp or a meat stock are all standard, and dried shrimp is a crustacean hiding in something that looks like plain rice. Which one is not published here. Ask.

items.en: Douhua — the same soy milk set soft into a silken pudding, served warm or cold with syrup and toppings
items.note: THE OTHER GOOD ONE. 豆花自体は豆乳を凝固させたもの＝植物性・小麦不使用。The pudding is soy milk and a coagulant — plant, no wheat. Everything uncertain about it is on top: peanuts, taro, tapioca pearls, adzuki and sweet syrups are the standard toppings, all of them plant, but Japanese kitchens sometimes add condensed milk. Ask what comes on it. Peanut is the allergen to watch here rather than gluten.

items.en: Peanut bing — a peanut-filled pastry, the cheapest item recorded
items.note: ⚠ 落花生使用。PEANUT, which is one of Japan’s eight statutory allergens and the reason to read this line at all. On gluten: 餅 (bǐng) in Taiwanese usage almost always means a WHEAT flatbread or pastry rather than a rice cake, so treat this as wheat unless the counter says otherwise — but the character can go either way and the shop declares nothing. Ask. Likely plant-based, though pastry lard is not unheard of.

tokyo_teuchi_soba_ozawa.price_note: ⚠ THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD INGREDIENT IN JAPAN IS ON THIS MENU AND THE SHOP DOES NOT DECLARE IT. Soba is buckwheat, buckwheat is not wheat, and a very large number of gluten-avoiding travellers conclude from those two true statements that a soba shop is safe. IT USUALLY IS NOT. Japanese hand-cut soba is conventionally 二八 — eight parts buckwheat to TWO PARTS WHEAT FLOUR, used as the binder that lets the dough be rolled and cut at all. Only soba explicitly sold as 十割 (jūwari, ten parts of ten) is pure buckwheat. 手打蕎麦 おざわ advertises itself as 手打ち, hand-cut, and says nothing about the ratio, so the default assumption has to be that there is wheat in the noodle. That single fact is worth more to a coeliac than any item on any menu in this batch. ⚠ AND THE SAUCE IS THE SECOND PROBLEM. そばつゆ is dashi, soy sauce and mirin: bonito (fish) plus wheat (soy). So even 十割 soba, dipped, is neither vegan nor gluten-free. A coeliac needs both the flour ratio AND the tsuyu answered; a vegan needs the dashi answered. ON THE LISTING: Tabelog publishes ONE item, ざる at 800円, undated, so this record is a placeholder with a firm structural warning rather than a menu. THE OPENING HOURS ARE THE OTHER THING TO KNOW AND THEY ARE SEVERE: Wednesday, Thursday and Friday only, 17:30–21:00 with last orders at 20:30, closed Monday and Tuesday and both weekend days. That is three evenings a week. 22 seats, 西浅草2-25-15.

items.en: Zaru soba — cold buckwheat noodles drained on a bamboo screen, served with dipping broth, with shredded nori over the top
items.note: ⚠ 手打ちそばは通常二八＝小麦粉2割を含む。十割の表示なし。The noodle is marked ask, not no, for one reason only: it MIGHT be 十割 and the shop has not said. Assume 二八 — 20% wheat — until told otherwise. Separately the つゆ is dashi, soy and mirin, i.e. bonito and wheat, so a vegan cannot use the dip even if the noodle turns out to be pure buckwheat. Two different questions, both needed.
